findings.title: ANY() over JS arrays will fail at query time
findings.body: Team and org authorization build `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` by interpolating a JavaScript array into Prisma.sql (lines 164, 168, and 201). Prisma binds that array as one parameter; through the query engine it is not a Postgres integer array, so PostgreSQL rejects the predicate (`operator does not exist` / invalid array literal) when these conditions are executed. User-scope SQL does not use ANY, and the only `$queryRaw` test is user-scoped, so the suite never runs the broken statements. Use `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or an explicit `ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[]` cast, and execute team/org conditions against the database.

findings.title: findMany removed; condition types changed to Prisma.Sql
findings.body: InsightsBookingService no longer exposes findMany(BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs), and getAuthorizationConditions / getFilterConditions now return Prisma.Sql instead of BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput. This PR only updates the service and its tests, so existing callers that pass a Prisma where/select into findMany, or that AND these conditions into a Prisma where object, will not compile and cannot query. Either keep a findMany wrapper that applies the SQL via $queryRaw, or update every caller in the same change.
